text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them and does not vouch for their accuracy.
POLITIKA
- Serbian Information Minister Radmila Milentijevic tells CNN her government is preparing new law liberalising media
- Yugoslavia's overall energy consumption will reach 1990 level only in 2005; high dependence on energy imports continues
- New accounting law delayed after experts clash over solutions to book-keeping problems
- Serbian government says school strike to end early this week; teachers' unions call for strike to continue
- Democratic Party of Serbia president Vojislav Kostunica says DSS will never join opposition Zajedno (Together) coalition
NASA BORBA
- U.S. congressmen welcome in Montenegro, Montenegrin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic says in statement issued in Washington
- Teachers' protests continue in Belgrade, more than half of all schools want to continue strike
- Opinion poll indicates most Belgraders want to continue democratisation protests initiated by Serbian opposition
- Serbian and Montenegrin opposition harmonise activities: media liberalisation one of key aims
- Montenegro could join IMF independently of Yugoslavia, says Montenegrin IMF expert Zeljko Bogetic
- Montenegro being harmed by Serbian authorities' complacency in regard to political problems, says privatisation agency director
- Opposition-dominated towns in Serbia to boycott state TV licence fees
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Still uncertain whether elementary and secondary schools will resume lessons on Monday. Teachers announce another protest outside Serbian government buildings.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Kosovo Albanian terrorist suspect hangs himself in prison during investigative detention
- Lola Corporation, machine tools and equipment manufacturer, plans to export $60 million in 1997, or 70 percent of total production.
- More than 120,000 employees in Serbia's health sector to stage one hour warning strike on Tuesday, demanding pay rise and back pay.
BORBA

- Radio Television Serbia, commenting on Montenegrin Prime Minister's critical statements on Serbia's regime, describes him as an "aggressive promoter and public relations agent of the ambitious and impatient pretender to the Serbian leadership, Serbian-born American Milan Panic".
- Croatia must guarantee Serbs' safety in Srem-Baranja region, says U.S. ambassador to Croatia Peter Galbraith.
